brief: Iran's Foreign Minister Araghchi proposed a seven-day plan to end hostilities (including in Lebanon), reopen the Strait of Hormuz and start comprehensive nuclear talks, compressing June's MoU sequence from 60 days to seven; under it the US would release at least $12bn in frozen Iranian assets, waive oil sanctions and lift the naval blockade before Hormuz reopens on the final day. Separately, SNSC secretary Rezaei said Iran will not return to the "Islamabad ceasefire" pace, gave the US 4-5 days to accept Iran's conditions (an implicit escalation threat), and warned neighboring states blocking Iranian flights that their airports would lose flights. Analyst Danny Citrinowicz cautions against dismissing these threats. The note lists factors favoring limited escalation over faster negotiation: a more aggressive Iranian military doctrine, a belief Trump is constrained by midterms, accumulating Iranian economic costs, the absence of a major US response near Hormuz, and Houthi pressure on Saudi Arabia giving Iran flexibility. Neither side wants uncontrolled war, but the note frames the next few days as a possible watershed, since economic pressure risks Iranian regime stability and Iran may ramp up pressure assuming only limited US retaliation.
